Device Hub Pro - Mirror, control and test Android emulators and phones, iOS simulators and iPhones side by side.

summary.one_liner: A free, open-source native Mac app that shows Android and iOS emulators, phones, simulators and iPhones side by side, with mirroring, control and device settings.
summary.what_it_does: Device Hub Pro mirrors Android emulators and phones and iOS simulators and iPhones on a Mac, with mirroring up to 60 fps and support for click, typing, rotation and hardware buttons. It lets you change device settings such as dark mode, text size, network, battery, location and language, and reads these values back from the device. A live log viewer can be filtered by app, level or text next to the device. It can create Android emulators from the Pixel catalog, with images downloaded in the background, and pair Android phones over Wi-Fi by QR code. It also captures screenshots, screen recordings, logs and crash reports, and manages apps by installing via drag and drop, launching, clearing data and opening deep links. The README says the app installs Google's Android tools itself, so Android Studio is not required.
use_cases: test an app on several Android and iOS devices at once
mirror and control an Android phone from a Mac
change dark mode, locale, or network settings on a simulator
view filtered live logs while running an app
take screenshots or screen recordings of a device
install, launch, or clear data for an app on a device
pair an Android phone wirelessly over Wi-Fi
how_to_run: Download the latest .dmg from the project's releases
Drag Device Hub Pro to Applications
Open the app; on first launch it sets up Android tools
For iOS simulators, install Xcode (touch and keyboard input verified with Xcode 27 on macOS 26.6 or later)
stack: Google Android tools (installed by the app)
notable: Shows Android and iOS devices side by side in one list
Installs Google's Android tooling itself, so Android Studio is not needed
Includes a sample iPhone Duo 3D view (Daybreak app in ios/duo)
Settings changes are read back from the device to confirm them
No accounts, analytics or telemetry, per the README
caveats: Requires macOS 15 or later on an Apple silicon Mac
iOS simulator touch and keyboard input need Xcode 27 (macOS 26.6 or later); older Xcode gives view-only simulators
Some iOS features rely on private Apple interfaces and may break after macOS or Xcode updates
